## Summary

**Investigation:** The source page is a minimal "lazy-loaded section" fixture — no `<style>` or `<link>` tags anywhere, so all rendering (h1 at 32px/700 weight, block-level p/div spacing, etc.) comes purely from default browser UA styles. windtailor against `body` confirmed this: no meaningful colors, custom fonts, or spacing tokens to extract — just browser defaults.

**JS-gated content:** The raw HTML only contains three empty `<div class="placeholder">` elements inside `#recommendations`. A `<script>` block uses `setTimeout(150ms)` to replace them with three `.product-card` divs (image + name + price) built from an in-page `products` array — a simulated client-side recommendations widget. crow-nester's post-JS outline confirmed this resolved state (three `product-card` blocks, ~326k px² combined, the dominant content on the page). Since the raw HTML already made the JS-swap mechanism explicit in its own comment and code, I didn't need a separate slowcure run — the source itself gave the complete pre/post-JS picture.

**Componentization:** red-twine flagged the three `.product-card`-shaped elements as a genuine repeating group (confidence 0.85, shared class, identical shape) — consistent with them being real recommendation cards, not coincidental matches.

### Priority list (established before writing code)
1. `#recommendations` product cards — largest rendered area on the page and the only substantive content once JS runs.
2. `h1` "Recommended for you" — second-largest/only other visible element, sets page identity.

**Build decision:** Given zero source CSS, I deliberately did *not* load Tailwind or add any classes — doing so (even just Tailwind's preflight reset) would have altered margins/font on `h1`/`p` and actually *reduced* fidelity versus the plain-HTML original. The clone reproduces the exact markup, inline script, and timing logic verbatim, keeping the `/product.jpg` hotlink reference as-is (per source).

**Fidelity check:** Screenshotted original (`original.png`) and clone (`clone-round1.png`) at matching 1280×900 viewport, both post-JS. `odiff` reported **0 differing pixels** (exit code 0) — pixel-perfect match on round 1, so no further iteration was needed.
